sentences.text:
The Court made the following:
 THE HONOURABLE DR JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA  CRIMINAL PETITION NO:06/2026 ORDER:
The instant Criminal Petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C)/under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') has been filed by the petitioner, seeking a direction to dispose of C.C. No. 459 of 2016 on the file of the learned III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Vijayawada.
2. Heard Sri Anguru Manohar, learned counsel for the petitioner/A.6 and Mrs.K.Priyanka Lakshmi,
learned Assistant Public Prosecutor on behalf of the State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner herein is A.6 and that the crime was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 420, 464, 468, 471, 474, 447,
506, and 427 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, and Section 82 of the Registration Act,
1908.

Learned counsel would further submit that though the crime was registered in the year 2012,
the Court has taken cognizance of the offences in the year 2016 and numbered the case as C.C. No.
459 of 2016, which is still pending on the file of the III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Vijayawada.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the petitioner further brought to the notice of this Court that A.1 is not appearing before the trial Court and that some of the other accused are also not appearing, due to which the matter is being adjourned from time to time.
6. Considering the submissions made by both sides, it is apposite to dispose of the present petition.
It is needless to say that speedy disposal of a criminal case is a fundamental right of the accused.
In the present case, the crime was registered in the year 2012, the charge sheet was filed, and cognizance was taken in the year 2016.
The matter has been pending before the trial Court for more than a decade, which has caused serious prejudice to the accused.

7. Accordingly, the learned Magistrate is directed to look into the issue and take appropriate steps in accordance with law in case any of the accused are not available, so as to proceed with the matter and dispose of the case as expeditiously as possible, without granting adjournments in a casual manner or on mere asking.
The learned Magistrate shall also inform the progress of the case to the Registrar (Judicial) on or before 01.02.2026.

As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
_________________________________________ Dr. JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA Date: 05.01.2026.
